segments.translation: Indescribable (brjod du med pa: avācya) and invisible (bltar med pa: adraṣṭavya),
segments.structure: no finite verb — 38–39 are a nominal predicate chain, the object of /rtogs/ in 40.
segments.note: /brjod du med pa/ = verb stem + terminative /du/ + /med pa/, the negated potential: "there is no expressing [it]"; likewise /blta-r med pa/ "cannot be seen".
segments.concepts: *brjod du med pa / bltar med pa* (Skt. avācya / adraṣṭavya) — standard apophatic epithets of the ultimate truth (paramārtha-satya) in Madhyamaka: beyond conventional expression (brjod pa) and beyond ordinary perception (blta ba), since it transcends the subject–object duality of saṃvṛti cognition; recurrent e.g. in the Laṅkāvatārasūtra.

segments.translation: immutable ('gyur ba med pa: avikāra) and uncompounded ('dus ma byas: asaṃskṛta)
segments.structure: continues the predicate chain; /'dus ma byas/ = /ma/ + past stem /byas/ with /'dus/ as complement (negated past participle).
segments.concepts: *'dus ma byas* (Skt. asaṃskṛta) — "uncompounded/unconditioned": in Abhidharma the phenomena not produced by causes and conditions (saṃskāra); here, in Madhyamaka usage, the ultimate nature (dharmatā/śūnyatā) as free from causal construction, against the saṃskṛta dharmas.

segments.translation: if a yogin (rnal 'byor pa: yogin) realizes that,
segments.shift: Lindtner 1981, DharmaMitra: temporal "when" for the conditional "if"
segments.structure: rnal 'byor pa =yis= [agent, ERG] · de [object, ABS — picks up 38–39] · rtogs [V] ~na~ [conditional] → protasis of 41.
segments.note: /na/ = "if" (realization as condition); "when" is grammatically possible as well (both §2.8).

segments.translation: the obstructions of affliction (nyon mongs: kleśa) and of the knowable (śes bya'i sgrib pa: jñeyāvaraṇa) are abandoned.

references.name: Lindtner 1981
references.text: *he abandons* the obstructions of defilement and cognizable *(kleśajñeyāvaraṇa)*.

references.name: DharmaMitra
references.text: The obscurations of afflictions and the knowable are abandoned.

segments.shift: Lindtner 1981: active, with the yogin as agent; and one compound, not two obstructions
segments.structure: [nyon mongs · shes bya'i sgrib pa] [ABS] · spangs [main verb]; agent (the yogin) implicit from 40, copula elided (verse).
segments.note: /nyon mongs shes bya'i sgrib pa/ — the two obstructions (kleśāvaraṇa + jñeyāvaraṇa) or a single compound? Doctrinally the pair; the Tibetan is one nominal string.  /spangs/ active ("he abandons") or resultative passive — ambiguous.
segments.concepts: *nyon mongs kyi sgrib pa / shes bya'i sgrib pa* (Skt. kleśāvaraṇa / jñeyāvaraṇa) — the two obstructions: the afflictive one obstructs liberation (mokṣa), the cognitive one omniscience (sarvajñatā). Only a buddha has removed both; śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas only the first. That realizing the nature of 38–39 removes both is a characteristically Mahāyāna claim.

grammar: This four-pāda verse (verse 9 in the treatise) consists of two predicate-attribute pādas (38–39) describing an unnamed referent (the paramārtha/dharmatā established in prior verses) followed by a conditional converb clause (40: rtogs + na) and its apodosis (41: spangs). The subject of the conditional (rnal 'byor pa) is marked ergative (yis) as agent of the transitive verb rtogs; the apodosis (spangs) has an implicit agent (the same yogin) and an implicit copula, both licensed by verse-register compression. The demonstrative de in pāda 40 anaphorically picks up the entire description of segments 38–39.
translation: Indescribable (brjod du med pa: avācya) and invisible (bltar med pa: adraṣṭavya), immutable ('gyur ba med pa: avikāra) and uncompounded ('dus ma byas: asaṃskṛta) — if a yogin (rnal 'byor pa: yogin) realizes that, the obstructions of affliction (nyon mongs: kleśa) and of the knowable (śes bya'i sgrib pa: jñeyāvaraṇa) are abandoned.

references.name: Lindtner 1981
references.text: [It is also] inexpressible (avācya) and invisible (adraṣṭavya), unchangeable (avikāra) and uncompounded (asaṃskṛta). *When* a yogi understands it *he abandons* the obstructions of defilement and cognizable *(kleśajñeyāvaraṇa)*.

references.name: DharmaMitra
references.text: Inexpressible and invisible, / Unchanging and unconditioned— / *When* a yogi realizes this, / The obscurations of afflictions and the knowable are abandoned.

comparison: Both read the realization temporally ("when"). Lindtner makes the yogin the agent of the abandoning and gives the two obstructions as one compound; DharmaMitra and the translation here read two obstructions and a passive result.
